title: Abelian covers, Gale correspondences, and the Hodge conjecture for powers
main_claim: (1) For a fixed connected topological abelian cover of curves, at every tensor-Hodge-generic point of the full marked variation, the rational Hodge conjecture holds on (Jac(C_s) x M)^N for every CM abelian variety M and every N, and on C_s^a x M^b. (2) For diagonal complete intersections cut out by c<=2 equations of degree n>=2, the Hodge conjecture holds on every self-power X_A^u for very general A in the smooth locus D_{c,m}. For c<=1 or d=0 this holds at every smooth parameter.

issues.location: Proof of Prop. 4.2 / Thm 1.1 (block assembly), paper.tex ~l.2471-2499, together with Prop. 4.14(ii)
issues.description: Two-dimensional non-toric blocks are always treated as 'linear', meaning a space V_i paired with its conjugate. On the sphere, an order-two character with dim W_chi = 2 has conj(W_chi) = W_chi, so the linear block is self-opposite: it is acting 'standardly on its own copies and dually on opposite copies' at the same time. This is consistent because SL2 = Sp2 and the standard module is self-dual, and the space could equally be put in a symplectic block with its polarization pair tensor. But the paper does not say which reading the companion saturated criterion (Comp. results 2.2(b),(c)) is meant to allow. This is a bookkeeping point, not a mathematical failure.
issues.evidence: "Treat a two-dimensional block as linear." ... "A linear block uses the polarization pairing of a character and its opposite."

issues.description: The final Hodge-class conclusion depends entirely on companion statements: the saturated determinant criterion [OpenAIAbelianPowers, Thm 2.5], correspondence transfer [Lemma 2.6], and the CM Hodge theorem [OpenAICM, Thm 1.1]. They are not proved here, and I did not audit them. The paper only supplies their hypotheses: determinant supply, standard projections, and Hodge-compatible links. This is a dependency, not a gap in this paper.
issues.evidence: "Saturated data imply that every rational balanced tensor is algebraic ... This is the saturated clause of [Theorem 2.5]{OpenAIAbelianPowers}."

coverage:
I read the whole LaTeX source (3779 lines) and checked the following in detail.
- Sec. 3: Fermat supply (Shioda-Katsura base locus and blow-up induction, the CM Fermat curve) and the faithful cyclic determinant lemma: the rank 2g+r-2, the Leray localization onto the Abel fiber |K_B(D)| in the branched and unramified cases, the A^{g-1}x(C*)^{r-1} decomposition, the Kummer splitting over the Fermat bundle Y, the dimension and degree bookkeeping (d=g+r-2, 2d-n=r-2, Gamma in CH^n), Deligne 8.2.5 weight detection, the return pairing and the idempotent sign.
- Sec. 4: the Hodge-generic locus with L° inside J_s; the rank-one-nilpotent classification; the twist cocycle formulas, including recomputing the [a_h,b_h] cocycle relation and the three-puncture twist displacement lying in U; the positive-genus cases; finite monodromy implying purity via the period differential; the infinite sphere monodromy case analysis; the sphere links for n>=3 (pair and triple products) and n=2 (Klein-four table, S'=S+2-a); mixed links.
- Sec. 5-6: smooth locus, Lefschetz, character ranks binom(s-2,d), evaluation quotient, the Gale perfect tensor (Lagrange identities, commutative square, exterior coproduct rank), Gale supply degrees, and codimension<=2 sources.
- Sec. 7: the branch-map normal form (I re-derived the Cramer formulas for t_i and z_i), the root family deck datum, the based marked comparison, tensor-generic loci via CDK, Cor. 7.7, the final assembly, and the Riemann-Hurwitz remark.
I did not audit the companion papers' proofs.
